# AI Usage Notes - Week 8 - Phuc Khanh

### **1. Scalable Settings and Compact Pause Menu**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** July 29, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Change the settings UI so that it scales with the game, add a Settings button
to the pause menu, and make the pause menu smaller in both dimensions.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To keep the settings popup aligned with the game's virtual resolution at every window size and make settings accessible without leaving a paused game.
* **Content generated by AI:** Moved settings drawing, hover detection, and button input into the 683x512 virtual UI coordinate system; added pause-to-settings navigation that preserves the frozen Hub or gameplay scene; added a Settings pause action and button; and reduced the pause container from 400x440 to 340x360 with compact controls.
* **Independent work/validation:** I required Settings Back and Escape to return to the pause menu when settings were opened from pause, while retaining the existing return to the main menu when settings were opened there. The unrelated existing deletion of `include/Entities/PathfindingEnemy.h` was preserved.

### **3. UI Rendering Optimization and Modal-Scale Refinement**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** July 31, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Review the current project and recommend UI rendering optimizations for
gameplay, dialogue, Pause, and Settings. Make Settings scale like Pause, add a
Settings button to Pause, reduce the Pause dimensions, and clamp modal scaling
so buttons remain moderate. Put the result in tmp. Revise the recommendation so
the team HUD is not refined because it is outside the current scope.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To define a consistent rendering architecture and a concrete correction for oversized modal panels and mixed UI coordinate systems.
* **Content generated by AI:** Created a detailed recommendation document with separate gameplay and modal scale policies, a maximum modal scale of 1.35, a dedicated SettingsMenu design, audio-slider migration, a compact 320x256 Pause layout, Pause-to-Settings navigation, background preservation, dialogue scale simplification, affected files, implementation order, and acceptance checks. The revised scope explicitly leaves the team HUD unchanged.
* **Independent work/validation:** I based the dimensions and physical-size comparisons on the current 683x512 virtual resolution and existing UI component sizes. I retained uncapped viewport scaling for gameplay-aligned UI, excluded team-HUD refinement, and used an upper-only modal cap so small windows can still shrink menus enough to fit. No runtime code was modified.

### **6. Hub Paladin Selection Plan**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** August 1, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Create a plan for a Hub Paladin selection feature: place all Paladins at fixed
positions around the Hub center; open a detailed selection UI with E while near
a Paladin; show a large character preview, comparable character and weapon
statistics with exact values, three team-slot assignment buttons, and two-step
Swap buttons that highlight the first choice and swap after the second choice.

Revise the plan so every displayed Hub Paladin is one `HubPaladinStand` class
spawned from character-specific IDs in the Game Objects layer. Remove legacy
map reading and migrate remaining runtime maps to layered CSV. Use the normal
gameplay idle sprite for the large center character and TeamHUD-style portraits
inside the slot buttons. Do not show ghost HP in Paladin selection.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To design a safe, scalable Hub workflow for inspecting Paladins and arranging the three-character team while moving Hub content to the project's layered object-map architecture.
* **Content generated by AI:** Created and revised Plan 9 with one object-layer `HubPaladinStand` class, separate Lance/Keith/Hunk map IDs, full migration away from the legacy text-map parser, proximity-based E interaction, normal gameplay sprites for the center preview, shared TeamHUD-style portrait buttons, comparable stats without ghost HP, duplicate-safe slot assignment, two-click highlighted swapping, active-character preservation, affected files, and validation checks.
* **Independent work/validation:** I based the revision on the existing `MapObjectId` values, layered filename convention, `EntityFactory`, TeamHUD portrait crop, loaded idle/weapon assets, and every current runtime reference to a legacy map. Assignment remains a move/swap because the current roster already contains Lance, Keith, and Hunk. No runtime code was changed.

### **9. Continuous Ranger Line-of-Sight Plan**

* **Tool:** Codex, GPT-5, OpenAI coding assistant.
* **Access time:** August 1, 2026.
* **Prompt used:**

```text
Create a plan to reduce Enemy Ranger randomness, make line of sight authoritative,
start visibility at the enemy while keeping bullets spawned at the gun, and
replace separated LOS probes. Assess a two-line corridor test and passing a
vector of object-pointer exceptions, then recommend the best approach without
making the project much more complex.
```

* **Purpose of use:** To eliminate wall-clipping Ranger shots and discrete LOS gaps while keeping the existing level-query architecture small and understandable.
* **Content generated by AI:** Created Plan 10 recommending continuous finite-segment collision against solid tile rectangles expanded by projectile radius, body-to-target visibility, body-to-muzzle clearance, validation of the final post-error muzzle path, deterministic direct/predicted target selection, a reduced one-degree aim error with zero-error fallback, private LevelManager helpers, unchanged LOS interface, and focused geometry/Ranger/Diver regression checks.
* **Independent work/validation:** I rejected an object-exception vector because current LOS does not include dynamic entities, and rejected a literal two-infinite-line implementation because it complicates end caps and rectangle corners. The recommended conservative expanded-AABB method reuses Layer 1, Layer 2, partial-wall, boundary, and destructible-box geometry without allocations or a new service class. No runtime code was changed.
